label: hv-mol-central-dogma
topic: Quantitative gene-expression statements: steady-state protein = synthesis/degradation, mRNA-protein correlation, burst statistics, Fano factor
summary:
Harvested 12 quantitative gene-expression statements from primary papers (abstracts opened via PubMed; full text opened for Taniguchi 2010 and Raj 2006). None of them is in the law registry: a grep of lean/**/*.lean, lean/laws.json, lean/registry/laws and tracks/lean for Fano|mRNA|gene expression|transcription returned no matches. tracks/research has hits for 'burst'/'degradation' only in materials and flying-fish agent files, which I did not open one by one.

Validated 5 predictions against reported numbers; 3 failed, 2 passed:
- Poisson mRNA (Fano = 1) vs E. coli: measured about 1.6. FAIL.
- Poisson mRNA vs a mammalian reporter gene: mean about 40, variance about 1,600, so Fano about 40. FAIL (bursty model consistent).
- Deterministic "protein proportional to mRNA" inside a single cell: predicts strong positive correlation; measured r = 0.01 +/- 0.03 (N = 5,447). FAIL at single-cell level.
- The same relation across genes (means): r = 0.77 by FISH (r^2 about 0.59), 0.54 by RNA-seq. PASS as a positive trend, far from exact.
- Gamma-distribution law for protein numbers: 1,009 of 1,018 strains fit (99.1%). PASS.
Also noted: the pure intrinsic gamma model (CV^2 = 1/a, falling without limit) fails at high expression, where noise plateaus at about 0.1.

Lean: D:/Users/ashenoy00000/delphi-work/agents4/hv-mol-central-dogma/CentralDogma.lean has 6 theorems (steady state p = k/d; two-stage mean; Poisson Fano = 1; bursty Fano = 1 + b > 1; gamma CV^2 = 1/a and Fano = b; variance proportional to mean iff CV^2 = B/mean). Run 1 failed on an environment error (could not read a Mathlib .olean.private file that does exist on disk; probably another process using the cache). Run 2, same file unchanged: ALL CHECKED, 0 errors, 0 sorryAx, 6/6 axiom lines. These are algebraic identities with the biology as named hypotheses; they do not prove the stochastic models themselves (no probability distributions are formalised).

Limits: the exact formulas for Thattai (Fano = 1 + b), Elowitz (noise decomposition), Paulsson and Schwanhäusser (R^2 about 0.4, model equations) are stated from memory of the papers; only their abstracts were opened, and the abstracts do not contain those formulas. The proposed open datasets (supplementary tables, GEO) were not opened. Based on articles retrieved from PubMed; DOIs are in the findings and citations.

findings.claim: S1. Steady-state protein level = synthesis rate / degradation rate. Formal: dp/dt = k_s - k_d*p; at dp/dt = 0, p* = k_s/k_d (assumes first-order loss, constant rates, dilution folded into k_d). Registry: absent. Falsifier: Schwanhäusser 2011 supplementary table (mRNA and protein copies, half-lives, >5,000 genes, mouse fibroblasts); test = across genes, log protein vs log(mRNA * translation rate * protein half-life) must have slope 1; note the paper derives translation rates from this model, so an independent rate (ribosome profiling) is needed for a real test.
findings.evidence_quote: cellular abundance of proteins is predominantly controlled at the level of translation
findings.confidence: Medium: abstract opened; model equation from memory of the paper; dataset not opened. Lean: steady_state_protein, checked.

findings.claim: S2. Two-stage model mean: m* = k_m/d_m, p* = k_m*k_p/(d_m*d_p). Formal as stated; assumes constant rates, one gene copy. Registry: absent. Falsifier: Li et al. 2014 E. coli ribosome-profiling synthesis rates (GEO, accession not verified by me) vs independent protein abundance; test = synthesis rate / dilution rate predicts copies per cell within a stated fold-error for stable proteins.
findings.evidence_quote: mean and variance of protein concentration can be independently controlled
findings.confidence: Medium: formula is standard, not in the abstract. Lean: two_stage_mean, checked.

findings.claim: S3. Protein Fano factor in the two-stage model: var/mean = 1 + b, with b = k_p/d_m (proteins made per mRNA lifetime), valid when protein lifetime >> mRNA lifetime. Registry: absent. Falsifier: Ozbudak et al. 2002 B. subtilis translation-efficiency mutants; test = Fano rises linearly with translational efficiency and stays flat with transcription rate.
findings.evidence_quote: noise is essentially determined at the translational level
findings.confidence: Medium: exact formula from memory, abstract supports the qualitative claim only. Ozbudak paper not opened. Lean: bursty_fano (algebra only), checked.

findings.claim: S4. Proteins per burst follow a geometric distribution: P(n) = (1-q) q^n, each burst from one mRNA. Registry: absent. Falsifier: Yu et al. 2006 burst-size histogram; test = chi-square goodness of fit of geometric vs Poisson burst sizes.
findings.evidence_quote: protein copy numbers in the bursts follow a geometric distribution
findings.confidence: High for the statement; dataset not opened.

findings.claim: S5. Burst size is exponentially distributed (continuous limit of S4); burst size and frequency recoverable from the steady-state copy-number distribution. Registry: absent. Falsifier: Cai et al. 2006 real-time beta-galactosidase traces; test = burst size and frequency from real-time traces must equal those fitted from the population histogram.
findings.evidence_quote: number of molecules per burst following an exponential distribution
findings.confidence: High for the statement; dataset not opened.

findings.claim: S6. Steady-state protein number is gamma distributed, p(x) = x^(a-1) e^(-x/b) / (Gamma(a) b^a), with a = k1/gamma2 (bursts per cell cycle) and b = k2/gamma1 (burst size); so mean = a*b, CV^2 = 1/a, Fano = b. VALIDATED: 1,009 of 1,018 E. coli strains fit = 99.1%. PASS. Registry: absent. Falsifier: Taniguchi 2010 supplementary per-gene table; test = fraction of genes whose single-cell histogram rejects a gamma fit.
findings.evidence_quote: 1,009 out of the 1,018 strains can be well fit by the gamma distribution
findings.confidence: High; the formula subscripts were partly lost in the page text. Lean: gamma_cv2_fano (moment algebra only), checked.

findings.claim: S7. Constitutive (Poisson) transcription predicts mRNA Fano factor = 1. VALIDATED against E. coli: measured about 1.6. FAIL (mRNA is not Poisson, even in bacteria). Registry: absent. Falsifier: Taniguchi 2010 FISH table for 137 genes (number recalled, not re-read); test = one-sided test that mean Fano > 1.
findings.evidence_quote: mRNA Fano factor values ... are close to ∼1.6
findings.confidence: High for the measured value. Lean: poisson_fano, checked.

findings.claim: S8. In mammalian cells mRNA is made in bursts, so Fano >> 1 (telegraph model: Fano about 1 + mean burst size when the gene is mostly off). VALIDATED: reporter gene mean about 40 mRNA per cell, variance about 1,600, so Fano about 40 against the Poisson prediction of 1. Poisson FAILS; bursty model consistent. A natural gene (RNA polymerase II large subunit) had variance over 50 times the mean. Registry: absent. Falsifier: Raj 2006 single-cell FISH counts; test = variance/mean with bootstrap interval vs 1.
findings.evidence_quote: the variance was roughly 1,600 molecules squared
findings.value: Poisson prediction Fano 1; measured ~40 (1600/40); FAIL for Poisson
findings.confidence: High for the numbers (Fano 40 is my division). The 1 + burst-size formula is from memory; the paper's numeric burst size was only in a figure I could not read.

findings.claim: S9. mRNA and protein copy numbers of the same gene in the same single cell are uncorrelated. Formal: Pearson r(m_i, p_i) about 0 across cells, when protein lifetime >> mRNA lifetime. VALIDATED: a deterministic p proportional to m reading predicts r clearly > 0; measured r = 0.01 +/- 0.03 (SEM, N = 5,447). The proportional reading FAILS at single-cell level; the statement itself passes. Registry: absent. Falsifier: any joint single-cell mRNA + protein count; test = r differs from 0.
findings.confidence: High. Golding 2005 (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2005.09.031) reports weaker correlation early in the cell cycle, so timing matters.

findings.claim: S10. Across genes, mean protein rises with mean mRNA but far from perfectly. VALIDATED: E. coli r = 0.77 (FISH), 0.54 (RNA-seq), so mRNA explains about 59% and 29% of variance in means. PASS as a positive trend; FAILS as an exact law. Mammalian cells: mRNA and protein levels correlate 'better than previously thought', while half-lives do not correlate. Registry: absent. Falsifier: Schwanhäusser 2011 table; test = R^2 of log protein vs log mRNA and of protein vs mRNA half-life.
findings.confidence: High for E. coli values. The widely quoted mammalian R^2 of about 0.4 was NOT verified by me.

findings.claim: S11. Protein noise scales inversely with abundance up to a floor: variance proportional to mean (CV^2 = B/mean) in yeast; in E. coli CV^2 proportional to 1/mean below about 10 molecules per cell, then a plateau near 0.1 from extrinsic noise. So the pure intrinsic gamma model (CV^2 = 1/a, falling without limit) FAILS at high expression. Registry: absent. Falsifier: Newman 2006 yeast GFP-library flow cytometry (>2,500 proteins); test = slope of log CV^2 vs log mean equals -1 and no floor.
findings.evidence_quote: the expression variance was approximately proportional to the mean
findings.value: CV^2 = B/mean, floor ~0.1 in E. coli
findings.confidence: High for the statements; datasets not opened. Lean: cv2_inverse_mean, checked.

findings.claim: S12. Total noise splits into intrinsic and extrinsic parts: eta_tot^2 = eta_int^2 + eta_ext^2, with eta_int measured from the difference between two identical reporter genes in one cell. And bursting is not universal: most constitutive yeast genes show small variation consistent with single, separated initiation events (near-Poisson), while PDR5 is bursty. Registry: absent. Falsifier: Zenklusen 2008 single-mRNA counts; test = Fano of constitutive genes vs 1, and PDR5 vs 1.
findings.source: https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1070919 (PubMed 12183631, abstract opened); https://doi.org/10.1038/nsmb.1514 (PubMed 19011635, abstract opened); https://doi.org/10.1038/nature02257 (abstract opened)
findings.confidence: Medium: the decomposition formula is from memory, not in the abstract.

key_claims: None of the 12 gene-expression statements exists in the Lean law registry (grep returned no matches).
The Poisson 'Fano = 1' law fails against data in both bacteria (about 1.6) and mammalian cells (about 40).
Within a single cell, mRNA and protein counts of one gene are uncorrelated (r = 0.01), although across genes the means correlate (r = 0.77).
The gamma law for protein numbers fits 99.1% of 1,018 E. coli strains, but its noise prediction breaks at high expression (plateau near 0.1).

lay_summary: A cell makes a protein by first copying a gene into a message (mRNA) and then building the protein from that message.
The simplest rule says the amount of a protein settles where making it and breaking it down balance, like a bathtub with the tap on and the drain open.
But cells make messages and proteins in random spurts, so two identical cells can hold very different amounts.
We checked the simple 'smooth and steady' rule against published counts and it failed: real cells were 1.6 to 40 times more uneven than the rule allows.
A better rule that includes spurts matched 99 out of every 100 bacterial genes tested, and a computer proof-checker confirmed the algebra behind six of these rules.

glossary.mRNA: The message copied from a gene that tells the cell how to build a protein.
glossary.protein: A molecule that does work in the cell, built from an mRNA message.
glossary.synthesis rate: How many molecules are made per unit of time.
glossary.degradation rate: The fraction of molecules broken down (or diluted by growth) per unit of time.
glossary.steady state: The level at which making and losing balance, so the amount stops changing.
glossary.half-life: The time it takes for half of the molecules to be lost.
glossary.variance: A measure of how spread out the counts are around the average.
glossary.Fano factor: Variance divided by mean; equals 1 for purely random, independent events.
glossary.CV^2 (noise): Variance divided by the mean squared; spread relative to the average.
glossary.Poisson distribution: The pattern of counts you get when events happen independently at a constant rate.
glossary.burst: A short spell in which many molecules are made at once, followed by a quiet spell.
glossary.burst size: The average number of molecules made in one burst.
glossary.geometric distribution: A pattern where each extra molecule in a burst is less likely by a fixed factor.
glossary.exponential distribution: The smooth version of the geometric pattern.
glossary.gamma distribution: A two-number curve (shape a, scale b) that describes protein counts when production is bursty.
glossary.telegraph model: A model where a gene randomly switches between on and off.
glossary.two-stage model: A model with two steps: gene to mRNA, then mRNA to protein.
glossary.intrinsic noise: Randomness from the gene's own chemical steps.
glossary.extrinsic noise: Cell-to-cell differences in shared machinery that affect all genes together.
glossary.correlation coefficient (r): A number from -1 to 1 saying how closely two quantities move together; r^2 is the share of variation explained.
glossary.FISH: A microscope method that lights up and counts individual mRNA molecules.
glossary.RNA-seq: A sequencing method that measures the amounts of all mRNAs.
glossary.ribosome profiling: A method that measures how fast each protein is being made.
glossary.constitutive gene: A gene that is on all the time.
glossary.Lean / Mathlib: A computer proof checker and its maths library.
glossary.axiom: A basic assumption the proof checker accepts without proof.
glossary.named hypothesis: An assumption written openly in a theorem instead of being hidden.
glossary.law registry: The project's list of formal laws already written down.

recommendations: Add a 'gene-expression noise' law family to the registry, starting with the Poisson Fano = 1 law recorded as FAILED (1.6 in E. coli, about 40 in a mammalian reporter) and the gamma law recorded as passing with a stated scope (low expression; fails above the extrinsic floor).
Before any nanopublication, open the papers' full text or supplements to confirm the formulas I stated from memory (Thattai Fano = 1 + b, Elowitz decomposition, Schwanhäusser R^2).
Download the Taniguchi per-gene supplementary table (small) and recompute Fano, gamma a and b, and the CV^2-vs-mean slope per gene, so the tests run on rows instead of reported summary values.
The Lean file proves only moment algebra; a real formalisation would define the birth-death process in Mathlib probability and derive the Poisson and negative-binomial stationary laws.
